episodes.185222: A strong upper level disturbance and a cold front combined with daytime heating to produce scattered thunderstorms.  Most were sub-severe and produced small hail.
episodes.185601: A strong cold front shifting across the region encountered an environment displaying deep moisture, modest instability and favorable shear supportive of severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
episodes.185602: A strong cold front shifting across the region encountered an environment displaying deep moisture, modest instability and favorable shear supportive of severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.185603: A strong cold front shifting across the region encountered an environment displaying deep moisture, modest instability and favorable shear supportive of severe thunderstorms across coastal waters.
episodes.186504: External feeding bands and moisture field from hurricane Tammy moving well east and north of the region reached the local islands. Additionally, a nearby TUTT and remnants of T.C. Sean also helped promote rain activity. Flooding reports where received as strong showers and thunderstorms affected the island leaving around from 2 to 5 inches of rain, particularly across Eastern Interior, E/SE, Western-Western Interior and South-Central Puerto Rico as well as the metro area. A funnel cloud was detected within this activity.
episodes.186579: A broken line of thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front during the afternoon. A few of the storms produced large hail and isolated brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.186658: Thunderstorms knocked down several trees and caused minor structural damage in Georgetown County, SC.

events.narrative: Multiple sources reported quarter to ping pong ball size hail from near the intersection of Cabin Creek Rd and Robbs School Rd, across Highway 11, to the city of Gaffney. The hail covered the ground in some locations.
Emergency manager reported a large piece of metal roofing blown off a building at the intersection of Railroad Ave and Walnut St.
Public reported quarter size hail in a couple of locations along the Golden Strip, including on Adley Way.
County comms reported power lines blown down on Potato House Rd at Wylie Rd and on Sherer Rd.
Law enforcement reported a very large tree blown down in the roadway at 1984 John Wells Road.
The public reported quarter to ping pong ball size hail in Hinesville, GA.
Law enforcement reported a tree down on power lines and a home at 521 Azalea Street. Structural damage was reported to the home.
Public reported a funnel cloud in front of El Malecon in Santa Isabel. This cloud did not touched the water or land. Thunderstorms were developing near the area.
Public reported (via Social Media) nickel to quarter size hail between York and Rock Hill.
Law enforcement reported wires blown down and two awnings blown off a business at 40 Butler Street.
Law enforcement reported traffic lights blown down at the intersection of North Coastal Highway and East Oglethorpe Highway.
Law enforcement reported 2 trees blown down on power lines at 47 Bernice Lane.
Law enforcement reported a tree down on a car at 44 Carriage Way.
A tree fell on a power line along Columbia Ave near Eagle Chase Ct in Chapin.
The Hampton County 911 Call Center reported a tree down at 2000 Lento Road.
Spotter reported pea size hail at US Hwy 521 and Jim Wilson Rd.
Spotter reported pea size hail along Hwy 6 near the Lake Murray Dam.
The Hampton County 911 Call Center reported 1 tree down on Hill Road.
Two spotter reports of pea size hail near Interstate 20 and Hwy 277.
Public report of pea size hail along Knox Abbott Rd and 9th St.
Pea size hail reported at the Camp Creek Fire Dept.
A Colleton County emergency manager reported 3 trees down at 4068 White Hall Road.

A vehicle with two people trapped was located in a flooded Virgilio Biaggi Rd. between Urb. Perla del Sur and Urb. Villa Grillasca. This road is adjacent of the flooded Las Americas Ave. Authorities where rescuing them at that moment. Radar estimated 1 to 4 inches of rain in the Ponce municipality around 6:30 pm.
Pea size hail reported at Buford Fire Dept.
Flood waters where affecting a residence in La Victoria St., near the intersection with California St., in Ponce. No one was trapped nor rescued.
Pea size hail reported on Youpon Dr in Red Bank.
Emergency Managers reported a Section of PR-2 in Ponce flooded near a McDonalds. Authorities where cleaning up drainage areas. No people trapped.
Flood waters affected a car in Calle Los Pompanos, near the intersection with PR-2 or Ponce Bypass, between km 225.6 and 225.3, in Ponce. No one was trapped nor rescued.
Flooding affected a car in Avenida Valle Real, near Calle Rafael Lugo Gonzales and PR-2 or Ponce ByPass (near km 225.6), in Ponce. Two adults were trapped, and rescued by Ponce Emergency Managers.
Flooding was reported in Calle Taino, east of Avenida Eduardo Ruberte, in Ponce. No one was trapped nor rescued.

Several reports of thunderstorm wind damage on and around Rose Hill Rd in Georgetown County. Multiple trees were knocked down, including a large tree down on a shed on the Quail Club property. An unconnected trailer was knocked over and a large barn door was blown in. The damage was indicative of straight line winds.
Flooding was reported in a residence in Calle Salvador Dijor, near Avenida Federal, in Sector Las Canitas, Ponce. No one was trapped nor rescued.

Four cars had people trapped in them due to ponding water on Avenida Las Americas in Ponce near a Tasty Chicken restaurant. The emergency manager reported that the flooding was above the tires of the trucks and his waist. Ave. Las Americas was closed as it was impassable from Tasty Chicken to La Secretaria de Recreacion y Deportes Building. The authorities have the Avenida closed. The people trapped were rescued.
